meta.title: Homeownership Affordability Model Registry (user-selectable)
meta.guardrail: "Best outcome" means best-matched to the actual buyer, product, and lender — NOT the model that shrinks the gap on paper. The engine must never auto-select the most permissive model and must attach the buyer-risk disclosure to any permissive result. A more permissive model shows more buying power by transferring risk to the buyer (higher payment burden, thinner equity, higher default exposure) and may fail a real lender/appraiser.
meta.household_size_note: Income is AMI adjusted by household size via HUD income limits by size (getIncomeLimits). household_size_default=4 preserves the current kernel output (backward-compat golden fixture maxAffordablePrice(100000,0.80)===289983). Smaller buyer households (typical of 1-2BR townhomes) have lower income limits, which increases the gap — do not leave this at 4 for a townhome study.
meta.price_measure_note: Compare against a jurisdiction-scoped, product-appropriate price: value (ZHVI/ACS B25077), closed sale (Redfin median_sale_price / CAR), or list (Redfin sale_to_list). For Fruita these converge ~ $486k-$494k; never substitute county for place, and never use an unsourced figure.

implications.who_it_fits: Early planning and below-market for-sale screening.
implications.gap_direction: Most conservative — largest gap. Reproduces today's kernel.
implications.buyer_risk: Low-risk framing; may understate real buying power for a strong buyer.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: Not a specific loan product; a planning proxy.
implications.when_not_to_use: When you know the actual first-mortgage product — use that model instead.

implications.who_it_fits: First-time buyers pairing a low down payment with down-payment assistance.
implications.gap_direction: Lower cash to close, but PMI and full price financed raise monthly cost.
implications.buyer_risk: Thin equity at purchase; PMI until 20% equity; sensitive to price declines.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: Common conventional 97/95 LTV path; verify PMI + DPA layering.
implications.when_not_to_use: When the buyer can put 20% down.

implications.who_it_fits: Move-up buyers with 20% down and little other debt.
implications.gap_direction: Most permissive — smallest gap. RISK-TRANSFER WARNING REQUIRED.
implications.buyer_risk: 43% back-end DTI is a heavy payment burden; assumes no other debt (rarely true). Do NOT present a permissive result as 'affordable' without this disclosure.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: Standard conforming underwriting; back-end DTI includes ALL debt — the tool must collect borrower debt or the result is optimistic.
implications.when_not_to_use: Screening/planning, or any buyer with existing debt not entered.

models.label: Federal FHA-insured (3.5% down)

implications.who_it_fits: Credit-constrained first-time buyers (Federal Housing Administration loan — NOT the Fruita Housing Authority).
implications.gap_direction: Very low cash to close; MIP raises monthly cost and does not fall off.
implications.buyer_risk: Lifetime MIP; leasehold/CLT eligibility rules apply.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: Verify current MIP and FHA leasehold/resale-restriction rules for the chosen land structure.
implications.when_not_to_use: When conventional or USDA is a better fit.

models.source: HUD FHA — VERIFY current MIP schedule

models.label: USDA Rural Development (0% down, income-limited)

params.income_limit_note: Hard income cap (RD income limits), site rural-eligibility, and resale-restriction compatibility apply.

implications.who_it_fits: Income-eligible buyers in USDA-eligible rural areas — Fruita/Mesa is likely eligible (VERIFY the specific site).
implications.gap_direction: 0% down removes the cash barrier; strict income caps limit who qualifies.
implications.buyer_risk: No equity cushion at purchase; guarantee fee adds cost.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: Verify site eligibility, income limits, and ground-lease/resale-restriction compatibility with RD.
implications.when_not_to_use: Non-rural sites or above the income cap.

models.source: USDA RD 502 Direct/Guaranteed — VERIFY current limits + Fruita site eligibility

models.label: Prop 123 DPA eligibility gate (not an affordability finding)

implications.who_it_fits: Prop 123 down-payment-assistance eligibility screening for households at or below 120% of either statewide or local AMI. This is an assistance-eligibility screen, not a burden or affordability test.
implications.gap_direction: Compare with conservative_screening (30% front-end) to see the eligibility-versus-affordability gap. The difference between the two is the useful output, not either number alone.
implications.buyer_risk: The 38% front-end gate exceeds conventional (28%), USDA (29%), and FHA (31%) standards, so a household passing this gate may still fail underwriting for the underlying mortgage.
implications.lender_appraisal_acceptance: SB26-040 raised the prior 35% threshold to 38% effective 2026-07-01. This program rule does not determine what a lender will write.
implications.when_not_to_use: Do not use as an affordability finding or mortgage-qualification result. The Division of Housing may modify the percentage by waiver where substantial housing need exists and a unit was marketed for at least 6 months without a purchaser, so 38% is a default with a documented exception path rather than a hard constant.

models.source_note: The enacted bill summary documents the 38% monthly-housing-cost gate, the statewide-or-local 120% AMI test, and the waiver path. The front-end characterization and 35%-to-38% change are also stated in the sponsor summary at https://www.senatedems.co/newsroom/legislation-to-create-more-affordable-home-ownership-opportunities-signed-into-law. The enacted-text PDF was not retrievable during research and was not represented as directly reviewed.

implications.who_it_fits: Advanced users / underwriters modeling a specific product.
implications.buyer_risk: User-owned; the tool still shows the risk disclosure if the entered ratios are aggressive.
implications.when_not_to_use: When a named product model already fits.
